classification.difficultyReason: Choose a similarity test, match corresponding sides despite changes in orientation, and justify equal ratios together with the required included or right angles. All necessary measurements and angle information are supplied directly.

content.prompt: State, with reasons, why these triangles are similar.

spec.description: Paired triangles with horizontal bases and opposite vertical sides. No right-angle markers.
spec.mathematics: AB=5 m, AC=12 m, BC=13 m; DE=10 m, DF=24 m, EF=26 m.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied labels are visible; no similarity reason is printed.

answer.short: SSS: three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, $5:10=12:24=13:26=1:2$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{AB}{DE}&=\frac{5}{10}=\frac12\\\frac{AC}{DF}&=\frac{12}{24}=\frac12\\\frac{BC}{EF}&=\frac{13}{26}=\frac12\end{aligned}$$
Three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ by SSS.

spec.description: An inverted triangle beside a smaller upright triangle.
spec.mathematics: Angle A=angle D=75 degrees; angle B=angle E=80 degrees. No side lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only given angles and vertex names are visible.

answer.short: AAA: $\angle A=\angle D=75^\circ$ and $\angle B=\angle E=80^\circ$; two pairs of corresponding angles are equal.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle A&=\angle D=75^\circ\\\angle B&=\angle E=80^\circ\end{aligned}$$
At least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ by AAA.

spec.description: Two oblique triangles, with AC and FD horizontal and equal included obtuse angles.
spec.mathematics: AB=5 m, AC=3 m, angle BAC=120 degrees; DE=10 m, DF=6 m, angle FDE=120 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: The given sides and included angles remain visible.

answer.short: SAS: $5:10=3:6=1:2$ and the included angles $\angle BAC=\angle EDF=120^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{AB}{DE}&=\frac{5}{10}=\frac12\\\frac{AC}{DF}&=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12\\\angle BAC&=\angle EDF=120^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and their included angles are equal, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ by SAS.

spec.description: Two right triangles with right-angle squares at A and D.
spec.mathematics: AC=11 m, BC=13 m; DF=22 m, EF=26 m. AB and DE are unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Given legs, hypotenuses and right-angle marks are visible.

answer.short: RHS: both triangles are right-angled, and $13:26=11:22=1:2$ for the hypotenuses and one pair of corresponding sides.
answer.worked:
$\angle BAC=\angle EDF=90^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{BC}{EF}&=\frac{13}{26}=\frac12\\\frac{AC}{DF}&=\frac{11}{22}=\frac12\end{aligned}$$
The hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ by RHS.

spec.description: A larger right triangle above left and a smaller right triangle below right.
spec.mathematics: EF=2 m, FD=4 m, angle DEF=90 degrees; BC=0.5 m, AC=1 m, angle ABC=90 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied dimensions and right-angle marks are visible; no missing lengths are added.

answer.short: RHS: both triangles are right-angled, and $4:1=2:0.5=4:1$ for the hypotenuses and one pair of corresponding sides.
answer.worked:
$\angle DEF=\angle ABC=90^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{DF}{AC}&=\frac41=4\\\frac{EF}{BC}&=\frac{2}{0.5}=4\end{aligned}$$
The hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so $\triangle DEF\sim\triangle ABC$ by RHS.

spec.description: Two separate triangles arranged diagonally with horizontal AC and FD.
spec.mathematics: AC=12 m, AB=6 m, angle BAC=40 degrees; DF=18 m, DE=9 m, angle FDE=40 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Given side lengths and included angles are visible; BC and EF remain unlabelled.

answer.short: SAS: $6:9=12:18=2:3$ and the included angles $\angle BAC=\angle EDF=40^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{AB}{DE}&=\frac69=\frac23\\\frac{AC}{DF}&=\frac{12}{18}=\frac23\\\angle BAC&=\angle EDF=40^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and their included angles are equal, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ by SAS.
